tldr: ToolTrain is a two-stage tool-integrated training framework combining rejection-sampled SFT and tool-integrated reinforcement learning that significantly improves LLMs' ability to perform Repo Deep Search for issue localization in code repositories.
contributions: Designed RepoSearcher, a lightweight issue localization agent with simple and easy-to-use retrieval tools
Proposed ToolTrain, a two-stage tool-integrated training approach combining rejection-sampled SFT and rule-based RL with nDCG@k reward
Constructed around 28k high-quality localization training examples from GitHub (issue, pull request) pairs
Demonstrated state-of-the-art performance among same-size LLMs, with the 32B model surpassing Claude-3.7 on function-level localization
methods: The authors designed RepoSearcher, an LLM-based agent equipped with six repository search tools (GetRepoStructure, GetImportOfFile, SearchClass, SearchFunction, SearchClassMethod, and Exit) for navigating code repos. They constructed ~28k training examples by pairing resolved GitHub issues with their corresponding pull requests from 600 high-quality repositories, excluding those in the SWE-Bench-Verified evaluation set. Training used a two-stage process: first, rejection-sampled supervised fine-tuning on high-quality tool-use trajectories that hit the ground-truth answer; second, tool-integrated reinforcement learning using nDCG@k as a rule-based reward signal to evaluate both recall and ranking quality of predicted functions.
results: ToolTrain-trained models achieve state-of-the-art performance on issue localization among same-size LLMs. The 32B model surpasses Claude-3.7 on function-level localization. Improved localization performance translates to better end-to-end issue resolution performance. The analysis confirms that RL effectively enhances the LLM's tool-calling and reasoning abilities, enabling more efficient and precise repository exploration.
limitations: The paper notes that excessive SFT fine-tuning alone risks compromising the model's generalization capabilities by causing the model to 'memorize' superficial patterns from a small number of successful examples
Ensuring the reliability of ground-truth answers for issue localization training data is identified as a difficult and underexplored problem
The training data was constructed from 600 GitHub repositories, which may limit generalization to other codebases
